reason: The cited evidence shows improved oxidation resistance for a thick (120 µm) Hf coating processed by hot pressing, not a thin sputtered HfO2 coating. The mechanism (sintering to form HfO2) and conditions (5 h oxidation, unspecified temperature) differ from the hypothesis, leaving key premises about sputtered HfO2 barrier properties and performance at 1300°C for 100 h unsupported.
premises: A thin HfO2 coating can be deposited on refractory HEAs via sputtering to form a continuous, dense barrier.
HfO2 is thermodynamically stable and acts as an impermeable oxygen diffusion barrier at 1300°C.
The HfO2 coating will significantly reduce oxidation rate (weight gain, oxide scale thickness) compared to uncoated alloy.
The coating will preserve mechanical strength by preventing surface degradation and spallation.
The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) demonstrates these effects for Hf-based coatings on VZrHfNbTa alloys.
